_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership (Jun-2026), moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for SAMIL. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026.

production.what: Q1FY27 global light-vehicle production -1.8% YoY (China -3.1%, the largest market); South Asia the bright spot (India LV +12.8%, India CV +16.2%); global CV production est. +5.4% on the North American recovery; 'planned European OEM launches expected to support growth' in FY27.
production.src: Q1FY27 PPT slide 7 (S&P Global Mobility, GlobalData) and call

commodities.what: LME copper USD9,519/t (Q1FY26) -> USD12,852 (Q4FY26) -> USD13,324 (Q1FY27), +40% YoY; aluminium +45% YoY; German polymer prices +55% YoY and +66% QoQ; World Container Index +40% YoY and +83% QoQ, all after the Middle East conflict. Pass-through: copper with a 3-6 month lag, polymers mostly settled at year-end.

fx.what: Rupee weakened ~13% vs the euro (Rs97.07 -> Rs110.03) and ~11% vs the dollar (Rs85.59 -> Rs94.66) between Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 (quarter averages). Most of SAMIL's revenue is earned abroad, so reported growth in rupees is flattered by translation.

europe.what: Europe (Germany 15%, Spain 6%, Hungary 6%, Poland 3%, France 3% of FY26 gross revenue) is SAMIL's biggest region; volumes 'not as meaningful as we have expected'; Chinese OEMs gaining share; supplier distress creates acquisition opportunities ('a record number of bankruptcies').
europe.src: Q4FY26 PPT slide 20; Q4FY26 call; Investor Meet 2025

consolidation.what: OEMs ask SAMIL to take over distressed suppliers (Nexans Autoelectric, Yutaka Giken from Honda, earlier Yachiyo and Atsumitec): 15 entities since Sep-2022 with pro forma revenue of ~USD2.8 bn before the two 2026 deals.

excluded.BHARATFORG: Earnings distorted: a Rs358 cr exceptional charge pushed the Jun-2026 quarter to a Rs90 cr loss (exceptional items in three of the last four quarters), so its trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 (~93x) sits on depressed TTM EPS.
excluded.GABRIEL: No five-year history: Screener's P/E series starts in May-2024 (after Gabriel's restructuring), so there is no five-year median to compare with.

peers.notes: Indian listed auto-component makers with Screener data (tyre and battery makers left out: different raw-material cycles). SCHAEFFLER (December year-end) has P/E history only from Feb-2023; MSUMI listed Mar-2022 and ZFCVINDIA's series starts May-2022: their medians cover the history available. MSUMI is 33.43% owned by SAMIL. Sector de-rating uses the set excluding SAMIL and the two names above (PLAYBOOK §7c).

street._note: Notes published 6-Aug to 30-Sep-2026 (after the Q1FY27 results on 6-Aug-2026). Ratings, targets and methods as reported; n.d. = not disclosed in our sources.

brokers.thesis: Outperformance of global auto, premiumisation and EV content, order backlog, acquisitions integrate; FY28E sales Rs1,75,832 cr, EBITDA 10.1%
Consumer-electronics third plant (41 mn units), CV recovery, order book; multiple raised from 21x; FY29E EPS Rs8.9
Revenue/earnings CAGR 16%/31% over FY26-28E; acquisitions, order book, content growth
European restructuring gains, rising non-auto share, lower cyclicality
Revenue +11%/+12%/+18% FY27-29F, above consensus; 6-7% FCF yield FY28-29F; operating leverage; acquisitions

consensus.note: A post-results consensus EPS dated before 30-Sep-2026 was not found.

Radha Rani Holdings Pte (promoter; 12 cr shares pledged)

stockEvents: Nexans Autoelectric and Yutaka Giken completed
Vision 2030 (USD 108 bn) unveiled at the Investor Meet
Prices and EPS restated by Screener
moat: Top-3 global mirror maker; India PV harness leader; supplier to every major OEM; USD96 bn booked business; OEMs hand it distressed suppliers to rescue.
Wins volume and acquisition opportunities others do not get.
No customer above 9% (VW), no country above 22% (India), no component above 25% (harness).
Lowers risk, but also means SAMIL is a play on global auto production, not a niche.
Commodity costs passed on with a lag; EBITDA margin 8-10% for a decade; OEMs negotiate annual price-downs.
Margins are capped; returns depend on utilisation and cost-cutting.
PKC, SMP, SMRC and Yachiyo turned around; but ROCE (company basis) only 16-17% vs a 40% target, and European plants still need restructuring (FY26 Rs379 cr).
Real skill, but the cost of buying growth is visible in returns.
Cameras, digital mirrors, lighting electronics, high-voltage harness; engine-agnostic (EV booked business 22%).
Content per vehicle rises with premium cars and EVs.
All 13-16 new plants in emerging markets; India, Mexico, Morocco, Eastern Europe.
Helps bids, not a barrier rivals cannot copy.
Consumer electronics 7.5x revenue growth in FY26 to ~Rs1,300 cr at ~8% EBITDA; customer concentration; aerospace order book USD1.6 bn.
critiques: Growth is bought: acquisitions and a weaker rupee explain most of FY27 revenue growth; organic volume growth in Europe is close to zero.
Returns are low for the risk: ROCE 13% (Screener) / 16% (company) against a 40% target that was also missed in Vision 2025.
Margins are structurally thin (8-10%) and lag commodity moves; Q1 is weak, Q4 carries annual settlements.
Consumer-electronics capex (~Rs7,500 cr) goes into one customer programme that management will not size.
Recurring 'exceptional' restructuring costs (FY24 Rs251 cr, FY26 Rs413 cr) flatter normalised profit.
Bulls: content growth, consolidation winner, India and non-auto give a growth premium; 6-7% FCF yield by FY28-29.

governance.board: Founder V.C. Sehgal is non-executive chairman (no remuneration from SAMIL); son L.V. Sehgal non-executive director; Pankaj Mital the only whole-time director; four of seven directors independent (incl. former SBI chairman Dinesh Khara from Sep-2025).
governance.auditor: S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP; unmodified opinion; KAM on impairment of Rs1,421 cr of PPE at loss-making European plants
governance.relatedParty: Large intra-group dealings with JVs (MSWIL, Kyungshin, Marelli Motherson) and promoter entities; promoter pledge 12 cr shares (Radha Rani)
governance.capitalAllocation: Serial acquirer (15 entities since Sep-2022 plus Nexans and Yutaka); capex ~Rs6,000 cr a year; payout 16%; QIP and CCDs in Sep-2024; leverage 0.8x
